brief: Destinations: Dubai Municipality and Emaar Malls signed a memorandum on 16 Oct to explore new commercial, community and lifestyle destinations on public land across Dubai; no sites have been named yet.

Türkiye: Torunlar GYO fixed the final price for Forum Kayseri AVM at EUR 131,904,579 (KAP, 12 Oct; Mall Report, 16 Oct), and WinsTown AVM in Diyarbakır handed its leasing to MSP; neither mall is in the Directory yet.
CX: Abu Dhabi launched TAMM Global on 16 Oct to license its AI-powered government services platform abroad, citing 94.5% customer satisfaction and service costs down 30%.

AI: Semafor reports that Amazon and eBay are blocking AI shopping agents ahead of the holiday season (16 Oct), and WEF and Bain put AI's value in MENA at more than $1 trillion by 2030, an estimate that covers finance, energy and the public sector rather than retail.

2027 Directory and watch: Arada's own figures put Madar Mall at Aljada at 1.1m sq ft GLA for December 2028, so it moves to the pipeline; King Khalid International in Riyadh reopened on 18 Oct, but several airlines keep Saudi suspensions into November.

findings.entity: Emaar Malls Management (destinations in public spaces)
findings.company: Emaar Malls Management LLC (Emaar Properties) with Dubai Municipality
findings.title: Dubai Municipality and Emaar Malls sign a memorandum to explore new destinations in public spaces
findings.summary: Dubai Municipality and Emaar Malls Management LLC signed a Memorandum of Collaboration on 16 October 2026 to explore future commercial offerings and community and lifestyle destinations across Dubai's public spaces and facilities. The two sides will share information on suitable and available locations, assess possible development opportunities and exchange expertise in commercial and destination development. No sites, number of locations, values or duration were published; the memorandum was signed by Eng. Bader Ahmed Anwahi, CEO of the municipality's Public Facilities Agency, and Ahmad Thani Al Matrooshi, Executive Director at Emaar Properties.
findings.why: It could open a pipeline of Emaar-run retail and leisure destinations on municipal land, worth tracking for the 2027 Directory and as a public-private model for MECSR members.

findings.company: Torunlar GYO (owner since 2 Feb 2026); Union Investment Real Estate GmbH (seller)
findings.title: Torunlar GYO sets the final price for Forum Kayseri AVM at EUR 131,904,579
findings.summary: Torunlar GYO has set the final price for 100% of Forum Kayseri Gayrimenkul Yatırım A.Ş., the company that owns and operates Forum Kayseri AVM, at EUR 131,904,579 after financial due diligence, against EUR 132,230,877.34 announced at first. The seller was Germany-based Union Investment Real Estate GmbH: the share purchase agreement was signed on 30 January 2026, the transfer completed on 2 February 2026 and the price was paid in cash. The update was filed on KAP on 12 October and reported by Mall Report on 16 October; neither gives the mall's GLA or store count, and Torunlar's H1 2026 activity report also records the purchase of Forum Mersin.
findings.why: It confirms a new owner for a regional Turkish mall that the Directory does not yet list, and adds a disclosed transaction value to Türkiye's retail investment record.

findings.company: Arada (developer); United Engineering Construction Company (main contractor)
findings.title: Madar Mall at Aljada: Arada's own figures give 1.1m sq ft GLA and completion in December 2028
findings.summary: Arada awarded United Engineering Construction Company (UNEC) an AED2.18 billion contract to build Madar Mall at Aljada, Sharjah, in a release dated 18 September 2025, with completion expected in December 2028. The Zaha Hadid Architects design has 1.1 million sq ft of GLA and 3.9 million sq ft of built-up area over three floors, with more than 400 shops, 80 dining outlets, an 11-screen cinema, an ice rink and a flagship fitness centre. This background answers the open question from Arada's 15 October 2026 release, which named Madar Mall among Aljada's continuing developments without figures.
findings.why: It moves a large Sharjah scheme from 'Check first' into the 2027 Directory pipeline with a primary-source GLA and target date.

findings.company: Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi (DGE)
findings.title: Abu Dhabi sets up TAMM Global to license its AI-powered government services platform abroad
findings.summary: The Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi announced TAMM Global on 16 October 2026, under a directive from Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi. The company will develop and manage the TAMM platform, hold its intellectual property and license its architecture and implementation methods to governments and organisations, which can adapt prebuilt services to their own legal frameworks. The National and Gulf News report more than 1,200 public and private-sector services, customer satisfaction of 94.5% (78% in 2022, before AI was integrated), service costs down 30% and about nine fewer service-centre visits per user a year.
findings.why: A Gulf government is now selling its customer-experience model as a product, which gives MECSC a citable satisfaction benchmark and a strong speaker lead for RCM Jeddah.

directory.headline: Service as an export: what TAMM Global means for customer experience
directory.angle: Abu Dhabi has set up a company to license its TAMM government services platform abroad, turning a customer-experience model into a product, with satisfaction and cost figures that malls and retailers can benchmark against.
directory.fits: MECSC customer-experience feature for the 2027 Directory or RPM · RCM Jeddah CX session
directory.facts: TAMM Global announced 16 Oct 2026 by the Department of Government Enablement, Abu Dhabi; more than 1,200 services; customer satisfaction 94.5% (78% in 2022); service costs down 30%; about nine fewer service-centre visits per user a year.
directory.caution: A photo caption in The National says more than 1,000 services: confirm the service count and how satisfaction is measured with DGE before print.

findings.company: Amazon and eBay; Cheq; Morning Consult
findings.title: Amazon and eBay block AI shopping agents as agent traffic climbs ahead of the holiday season
findings.summary: Semafor reported on 16 October 2026 that Amazon and eBay have blocked AI shopping agents to protect their advertising businesses and checkout experiences, as online retailers prepare for the holiday season. Cheq, a cybersecurity company that verifies AI shopping agents, told Semafor of a 100x surge in agentic traffic over a 45-day period after new consumer AI agents were released; this is a vendor figure and its method was not given. Morning Consult research cited in the piece finds shoppers about as likely to be swayed by an agent's recommendation as by an influencer's, though few are comfortable letting AI buy for them.
findings.why: Gulf retailers and mall e-commerce teams face the same choice between blocking and courting AI agents that global marketplaces are now making.

findings.entity: Unlocking Value: AI for Resilient Growth in MENA
findings.company: World Economic Forum with Bain & Company
findings.title: WEF and Bain: AI could unlock more than $1 trillion of economic and sustainability value in MENA by 2030
findings.summary: The World Economic Forum published 'Unlocking Value: AI for Resilient Growth in MENA', developed with Bain & Company, on 14 October 2026 in Dubai, alongside a data-centre infrastructure report produced with SRMG. The estimate of more than $1 trillion by 2030 is made up of up to $200 billion of sustainable financing, $370 billion of public-sector-enabled sustainable investment, $250 billion of long-term asset losses avoided, $90 billion of higher energy-sector valuations and $100 billion of cross-sector projects. In a survey of the MENA Chief Sustainability Officers Network, 89% saw high or very high potential for AI, but only 40 to 55% said their use cases were at the pilot or scaled stage; the release gives no retail or consumer figures.
findings.why: It is a citable regional AI headline for MECSR content, provided it is quoted with its scope: finance, energy, the public sector and sustainability, not retail.

findings.title: Apparel Group's AIVI app, the successor to 6thStreet, adds an AI stylist and virtual try-on
findings.summary: Apparel Group launched AIVI in August 2026 as 'the evolution of 6thStreet', one platform for its brands with Club AIVI rewards, citing more than 2,600 stores and over 85 international brands in 14 countries. Gulf News (updated 8 October 2026) describes an 'Ask AIVI' adviser that takes spoken or typed requests and suggests items from preferences, past searches and purchases, a virtual try-on from a photo or selfie, and Club AIVI, the renamed Club Apparel, which works across online platforms, stores and food and beverage outlets. The app is available in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman, with selected products delivered in as little as 60 minutes in the UAE.
findings.why: One of the largest fashion tenants in Gulf malls now runs discovery, try-on and loyalty through a conversational AI app that links online and in-mall stores.
